Müşterileriniz ile asla doğrudan temas kurmuyoruz; dilerseniz ajansınızın kurumsal e-posta adresiyle veya tamamen görünmez bir arka plan mühendislik masası olarak projelerinizi teslim ediyoruz. Tüm kaynak kodlar ve fikri mülkiyet hakları %100 ajansınıza aittir. Projeyi yürüten kişi ulaşılamaz olursa ne oluyor? TMA bir şahıs işletmesidir, ancak kriz masası tek kişilik değildir: masada ikinci bir kıdemli mühendis bulunur ve başlayan bir işi o devralır. Kod hiçbir aşamada bizde tutulmaz — repo sizin kontrolünüzdedir, dokümantasyon iş ilerledikçe teslim edilir. Çalışma yarıda kesilse bile ajansınızın elinde çalışan sistem ve eksiksiz kaynak kod kalır. Acil kod kurtarmada süreç nasıl işliyor? Canlı sistem kesintilerinde (HTTP 500, veritabanı kilitlenmesi, ödeme API kopması) önce repoyu izole bir sandbox ortamına alır, teşhisi orada yaparız. Teşhis ve sabit bedel birlikte iletilir. Süre taahhüdü vermiyoruz — her arızanın kapsamı farklıdır ve tutulamayacak bir söz vermek işe yaramaz. Acil bir durumda ne kadar sürede dönüş alırım? Kriz hattı her gün 09:00 – 24:00 arasında açıktır. Canlı kesinti (SEV-0) bildirimlerinde ilk yanıt taahhüdümüz 15 dakikadır; diğer seviyelerin süreleri SLA sayfasında yazılıdır. Bu saatler dışında ulaşan bildirimler ertesi sabah 09:00'da ele alınır. Yarım kalan veya dokümantasyonsuz spagetti projeleri nasıl devralıyorsunuz? Önceki geliştiricinin devretmeden ayrıldığı projelerde; repoyu klonlayarak mimariyi, veri modellerini ve kilitlenen noktaları haritalandırıyoruz. Eksik kalan backend uçlarını tamamlayıp, spagetti kodu modern standartlara refactor ederek dokümante edilmiş şekilde teslim ediyoruz. Geliştirilen kodların ve sistemin fikri mülkiyeti (IP) kime ait olur? Geliştirilen tüm kaynak kodlar, veritabanı şemaları, API konfigürasyonları ve dokümantasyon %100 sizin ajansınıza ve müşterinize aittir. Herhangi bir telif, lisans veya bağımlılık hakkı talep edilmez. Hangi teknoloji yığınlarında (Tech Stack) uzman desteği veriyorsunuz? Modern web ve backend dünyasının lider teknolojileri: React, Next.js, Node.js, Python / FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, Flutter, Stripe / iyzico ödeme webhookları ve OpenAI / LLM yapay zeka agent entegrasyonlarında kıdemli mühendislik desteği sağlıyoruz. Frequently Asked Questions How does Trend Master Akademi's White-Label partnership model work? We operate under a legally binding Mutual NDA. We never contact your clients directly; we build either under your agency's domain email or as an invisible backline engineering squad. All source code and IP rights belong 100% to your agency. What happens if the engineer running my project becomes unavailable? TMA is a sole proprietorship, but the response desk is not a one-person operation: a second senior engineer is on the desk to take over any work already under way. Your code is never held by us either — the repository is under your control and documentation is delivered as the work progresses. Even if an engagement is interrupted, your agency is left with a working system and the complete source. How does the emergency code rescue process work? For live production outages (HTTP 500, database deadlocks, payment API failures), we first isolate the repository into a sandbox environment and perform the diagnosis there. Diagnosis and fixed fee are delivered together. We do not provide time commitments — the scope of each incident differs, and making promises that cannot be kept helps no one. How quickly will I get a response in an emergency? The response desk is open daily between 09:00 and 24:00 (UTC+3). For live-outage (SEV-0) incidents our first-response commitment is 15 minutes; times for other levels are listed on the SLA page. Notifications arriving outside these hours are picked up at 09:00 the next morning. How do you take over undocumented or abandoned spaghetti codebases? For stranded projects left without handover; we clone the repository and map architecture, data models, and bottlenecks. We complete missing backend endpoints, refactor tangled spaghetti code to modern standards, and hand over a documented production release. Who owns the intellectual property and source code of the project? 100% of all developed source code, database schemas, API configurations, and documentation belong exclusively to your agency and client. Zero recurring vendor-lock or licensing claims. Which technology stacks do you provide senior engineering support for? Leading modern web & backend technologies: React, Next.js, Node.js, Python / FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, Flutter, Stripe / iyzico webhook architectures, and enterprise OpenAI / LLM agent automations. Technical Glossary — 12 Terms → Deadlock Critical (P0) A situation where two database transactions mutually block each other by holding locks that the other requires, freezing queries. → N+1 Query Problem Medium / High An ORM efficiency bottleneck where the application executes 1 initial query plus N additional queries for child records instead of a single batch query. → Race Condition Critical (P0) A concurrency flaw where multiple threads or requests execute operations out of anticipated order, causing data corruption. → Idempotency High A mathematical and API principle ensuring identical requests executed multiple times yield the exact same result without duplicate side-effects. → Webhook Critical (P0) An automated user-defined HTTP POST callback triggered by external service events like completed transactions or SMS deliveries. → Technical Debt Medium / Strategic The implied long-term cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy, fast software shortcut over a sustainable architectural design. → Refactoring Medium The process of restructuring existing computer code without changing its external behavior to improve non-functional attributes. → CI/CD Pipelines High A combined automation pipeline (Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment) that builds, tests, and deploys code changes seamlessly. → Staging Environment Medium An isolated pre-production environment that mirrors the exact production infrastructure, databases, and dependencies for QA. → Database Migration High Programmatic, version-controlled scripts that modify database schemas safely across different developer and production environments. → Rate Limiting High A defensive network strategy limiting the frequency of requests a client or bot can send to an API endpoint within a given time window. → Memory Leak Critical (P0) A programming defect where dynamically allocated memory is never released by the application, steadily degrading RAM until crash. Our Story & Founding Origins This business actually started in an online class. I spent twenty years inside financial markets. Software was always inseparable from that work — but for a long time only for myself: I wrote my own systems, turned my own ideas into code, debugged my own mistakes. I didn't work for anyone else, and I didn't want to. For twenty years I believed this was a one-person job, that I only ever needed to be enough for myself. In 2020, when COVID stopped everything and everyone was talking about scarcity, I started teaching what I knew. I ended up training around fifty people. Teaching changed me: having to turn twenty years of instinct into something another person could follow changed everything, bringing discipline to what had been scattered. The idea for Trend Master Akademi was born in those online classes. That is where our name comes from, and we never changed it. After partnering with one of those students, we both saw that the real need was in the field, not the classroom. Digital agencies were facing a severe bottleneck of qualified software engineers. Abandoned codebases, lost credentials, missed delivery deadlines, and escalating crises... We took over these troubled projects and brought them to completion one by one. That is what we do today: we are not an end-client agency. We are a senior engineering back-office operating 100% white-label behind digital agencies, software houses, and startups to resolve production crises and build resilient architectures. Our name remains "Akademi" — because rescuing a system requires understanding it deeply enough to explain it. Our Technical Glossary and Diagnostic Catalog are published with this exact philosophy. Ödemede gecikme hâlinde TMA, çalışmayı askıya alma hakkına sahiptir; askı süresi teslim süresine eklenir. MADDE 9 — FİKRİ MÜLKİYET VE MALİ HAKLARIN DEVRİ 9.1. TMA tarafından işbu sözleşme kapsamında üretilen ve 5846 sayılı FSEK anlamında eser niteliği taşıyan yazılım, kod, dokümantasyon ve tasarımlar üzerindeki mali haklar, bedelin tamamı ödendiği anda, süresiz, yer ve sayı bakımından sınırsız olarak AJANS'a devredilir. 9.2. Devredilen mali haklar şunlardır ve bunlarla sınırlıdır: a) İşleme hakkı (FSEK m.21) b) Çoğaltma hakkı (FSEK m.22) c) Yayma hakkı (FSEK m.23) d) Temsil hakkı (FSEK m.24) e) İşaret, ses ve/veya görüntü nakline yarayan araçlarla umuma iletim hakkı (FSEK m.25) 9.3. AJANS, devraldığı hakları üçüncü kişilere devredebilir ve alt lisans verebilir. 9.4. Devir, bedelin tamamının ödenmesi şartına bağlıdır. Ödeme tamamlanana kadar mali haklar TMA'da kalır; AJANS'a bu süre boyunca yalnızca test ve değerlendirme amaçlı kullanım izni verilmiştir. 9.5. TMA'nın kendisine ait kalanlar: TMA'nın işbu sözleşmeden önce geliştirdiği veya sözleşmeden bağımsız olarak geliştirdiği genel amaçlı araçlar, kütüphaneler, kontrol listeleri, şablonlar ve çalışma yöntemleri devir kapsamı dışındadır. Bunlar teslim edilen işte kullanılmışsa, AJANS'a bu iş özelinde süresiz, münhasır olmayan, devredilebilir kullanım hakkı tanınır. 9.6. Üçüncü taraf açık kaynak bileşenler kendi lisans koşullarına tabidir; TMA bu bileşenlerin lisans uyumluluğunu teslim raporunda belirtir. MADDE 10 — DEVRALINAN KOD VE MEVCUT KUSURLAR 10.1. TMA'nın devraldığı veya müdahale ettiği kod tabanı, üçüncü kişiler tarafından üretilmiş olabilir. TMA, kendi müdahalesinden önce var olan kusurlardan, güvenlik açıklarından, lisans ihlallerinden ve veri kayıplarından sorumlu değildir. 10.2. TMA'nın sorumluluğu, fiilen üzerinde çalıştığı ve İş Emri'nde tanımlanan kapsamla sınırlıdır. 10.3. AJANS, TMA'ya devrettiği kod, veri ve erişimler üzerinde tasarruf yetkisine sahip olduğunu beyan eder. Üçüncü kişi haklarının ihlalinden doğan talepler AJANS'a aittir. 10.4. TMA, teşhis aşamasında tespit ettiği ancak kapsam dışında kalan kusurları yazılı olarak bildirir; bildirimden sonra bu kusurların giderilmemesinden doğan sonuçlardan sorumlu tutulamaz. 10.5. Yedekleme: Müdahale öncesi yedek alınması AJANS'ın sorumluluğundadır. AJANS talep ederse TMA yedekleme desteği verir; bu destek ayrıca fiyatlanabilir. MADDE 11 — SORUMLULUK VE SINIRLARI 11.1. TMA, hizmetleri mesleki özen ve basiretli bir tacir gibi yürütür. 11.2. TMA'nın işbu sözleşmeden doğan toplam sorumluluğu, ilgili İş Emri kapsamında fiilen ödenen bedeli aşamaz. 11.3. TMA, dolaylı zararlardan — kâr kaybı, iş kaybı, itibar kaybı, veri kaybı, üçüncü kişi talepleri — sorumlu değildir. 11.4. Bu maddedeki sınırlamalar, TMA'nın kastından ve ağır kusurundan doğan sorumluluğu kapsamaz. Bu hâllerde genel hükümler uygulanır. 11.5. TMA, AJANS'ın veya müşterisinin altyapı sağlayıcılarından, üçüncü taraf servislerden veya ödeme kuruluşlarından kaynaklanan kesinti ve arızalardan sorumlu değildir. MADDE 12 — PERSONEL AYARTMA 12.1. Taraflar, sözleşme süresince ve sona ermesinden itibaren 1 (bir) yıl boyunca, diğer Tarafın projede fiilen görev almış çalışanına veya alt yüklenicisine doğrudan iş teklifinde bulunmaz. Kamuya açık ilanlara yapılan başvurular bu hükmün dışındadır. MADDE 13 — SÜRE VE FESİH 13.1. İşbu sözleşme imza tarihinde yürürlüğe girer ve Taraflardan biri 30 gün önceden yazılı bildirimle feshedene kadar yürürlükte kalır. 13.2. Fesih, devam eden İş Emirlerini etkilemez; bunlar kendi koşullarına göre tamamlanır. 13.3. Gizlilik (Madde 4), temas yasağı (Madde 5.2), fikri mülkiyet (Madde 9) ve sorumluluk (Madde 11) hükümleri fesihten sonra da yürürlükte kalır. 13.4. Haklı sebeple derhal fesih hakkı saklıdır. MADDE 14 — MÜCBİR SEBEP 14.1. Doğal afet, salgın, savaş, siber saldırı, ülke çapında altyapı kesintisi ve benzeri, Tarafların kontrolü dışındaki olaylar mücbir sebep sayılır. Mücbir sebep süresince yükümlülükler askıya alınır; 30 günü aşarsa her Taraf sözleşmeyi feshedebilir. MADDE 15 — MUHTELİF HÜKÜMLER 15.1. Tebligat: Madde 1'deki e-posta adresleri geçerli tebligat adresi sayılır. Adres değişikliği 7 gün içinde bildirilir. 15.2. Devir: Taraflar, diğerinin yazılı onayı olmaksızın sözleşmeyi devredemez. 15.3. Bölünebilirlik: Bir hükmün geçersizliği diğerlerini etkilemez. 15.4. Bütünlük: İşbu sözleşme ve İş Emirleri, Taraflar arasındaki anlaşmanın tamamını oluşturur. 15.5. Değişiklik: Değişiklikler yazılı olarak yapılır. MADDE 16 — UYGULANACAK HUKUK VE YETKİ 16.1. İşbu sözleşme Türk hukukuna tabidir. 16.2. Uyuşmazlıklarda İzmir Mahkemeleri ve İcra Daireleri yetkilidir. 16.3. Taraflar dava yoluna başvurmadan önce 30 gün iyi niyetle uzlaşmaya çalışır. Integrations & Rate Limits SEV-1 HIGH · MTTA: 30 Minutes Third-party API (shipping, SMS, ERP, marketplace) returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests; pending jobs blocking worker queues. The prototype works; but at launch, or at the first serious bug, it landed on your desk. Before you build on this code, tmai finds where it is safe and where it is not, and turns it into code you can take over. When is it tmai? • The client had the prototype built with an AI tool, and now it is opening to real users. • There is no developer who wrote the code; there is only the project the tool generated and an account. • Every new request breaks an earlier feature, and nobody knows why. • Payments, sign-up or personal data are about to go live, and you are not sure they are secure. What we check first These six areas are where a project quickly generated with AI tools needs to be checked before anything is built on top of it. Keys embedded in the browser API keys and secret keys may be written into the front-end code. Anything sent to the browser can be read by a visitor. What we check: Traces of keys in the built front-end files and in the repository; which keys must be moved server-side and rotated. Database rules left open In hosted database services such as Supabase or Firebase, access rules may be switched off or left open to everyone. What we check: Who can read and write each table or collection; data reachable directly from the front end. Authentication only in the front end If the login check exists only in the interface, someone who skips the page and sends the request directly can reach protected data. What we check: Whether every protected action is also authorized on the server side. No tests A generated project may have no automated tests; what a change breaks is only seen in production. What we check: Whether critical flows such as sign-up, payment and ordering have tests; if not, which flows get tests first. Duplicated logic Code doing the same job may be repeated across files, unaware of each other; a bug fixed in one place lives on in another. What we check: Whether rules such as pricing, permissions and stock live in one place or are scattered. Packages that do not exist, or are outdated AI tools can add a package name that does not exist, or an old version with a known security flaw. What we check: That every dependency actually exists, its version, and its known vulnerabilities. How it works 1 Pre-assessment → In the Handover Audit, tick "The project was built with AI tools" and fill in the 12 items. Missing access shows up from the start. 2 Confidentiality → Before we look at the code, the confidentiality and engagement agreement is signed. 3 Review The six areas above are checked on the project's own repository and accounts; the result is shared with the agency in writing. 4 Decision → With the Salvageability Index, we decide together whether the code is repaired and kept, or its critical parts are rewritten. 5 Intervention Keys, database rules and permissions first; then tests and simplification. A rollback point is taken before every intervention. Scope of intervention The AI tool itself, the hosting service and the database service belong to their providers. tmai works on the code and configuration in your accounts. Whether you keep using the tool is your decision. Tool names are mentioned only as examples; we have no partnership with these tools. One customer requires a refund. This symptom stems from three distinct root causes, each demanding a completely different fix — addressing the wrong one will cause the defect to recur. Urgency: Critical · revenue loss · Category: Orders & Payments Field Observations Usually appears during flash sales or immediately after an email campaign drops. Two separate orders for the final single unit are confirmed in the exact same second. Inventory drops to negative one; the first to notice is the customer whose order gets canceled. Observed System Error Signatures SQLSTATE[40001]: Serialization failure: 1213 Deadlock found → A · Race condition Duplicate entry '...' for key 'orders_reference_unique' → B · Missing idempotency UPDATE products SET stock = stock - 1 <- check and write separated Which of these lines appears in your error logs narrows down the exact root cause at first glance. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Race condition Two simultaneous requests decremented stock concurrently. There is an unisolated gap between check and write. Differential test: Are order created_at diffs < 1 second? Evidence: created_at diff < 1s → A Resolution: Atomic UPDATE + affected rows validation Common anti-pattern fix: Adding an if (stock > 0) check in application code fails because concurrent requests pass the check in the same millisecond. B · Missing idempotency A single payment was processed twice; either the customer double-clicked or a webhook redelivered. No concurrency, just duplication. Differential test: Are payment reference IDs identical? Evidence: payment_reference same → B Resolution: unique index + idempotency key lock Common anti-pattern fix: Failing to acknowledge the webhook promptly causes the payment gateway to retry after timing out, triggering duplicate order processing. C · Inventory sync lag Inventory master resides in an ERP or marketplace. The race is not on-site, but within sync lag intervals. Differential test: Was last ERP sync before order timestamp? Evidence: Sync older than sale → C Resolution: Reservation lock + higher sync frequency Common anti-pattern fix: Reducing cron intervals from five minutes to one minute fails because slow API responses cause queue congestion and unhandled conflicts. Who resolves it Senior backend engineer. Scope, timeline and budget become clear after diagnosis. Once the exact cause is isolated, all three are permanently resolved. Fixes applied without proper diagnosis merely mask symptoms while leaving the root cause intact. Impact If Left Unresolved Every oversold item triggers refund overhead, double logistics costs, and negative client feedback. Under high-traffic sales campaigns, frequency compounds exponentially. The client contacts support with no reference on file. Funds are in the bank, order is missing — caused by a severed webhook callback between the two. Urgency: Critical · commercial loss · Category: Orders & Payments Field Observations The customer sees the charge on their card statement and receives the bank confirmation SMS. However, their cart remains full, no order confirmation displays, and no record appears in admin. The crisis starts when they call support. Observed System Error Signatures Webhook endpoint: 404 / 500 / timeout Payment gateway panel: callback failed · retry 3/3 → A · Callback undelivered App logs contain no trace of payment reference HTTP 302 - notification fails to follow redirect → A · Callback undelivered Every webhook dispatch attempt is logged in the payment gateway dashboard. Checking provider logs is faster than codebase debugging: it reveals retry counts and HTTP response codes directly. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Callback undelivered Gateway sent webhook but endpoint URL was invalid, firewalled (WAF), or blocked. Differential test: Are webhook retry logs visible in gateway panel? Evidence: 404 or timeout in gateway panel → A Resolution: Fix endpoint URL + whitelist WAF Common anti-pattern fix: Asking the customer to reorder fails because mismatched bank authorizations create unresolved reconciliation discrepancies in accounting. B · Callback unhandled (500) Webhook arrived but application threw unhandled exception. Retries repeated the crash. Differential test: Did webhook arrive but throw 500 fatal error? Evidence: HTTP 500 + retry loop in logs → B Resolution: Patch exception + queue job buffer Common anti-pattern fix: Returning an empty 200 OK to swallow webhook errors halts provider retries, causing the missing order to vanish permanently. C · Validation drop (Silent 200) Webhook returned HTTP 200 but order insertion failed silently due to internal validation drops. Differential test: Was 200 returned without creating order record? Evidence: HTTP 200 returned but no row → C Resolution: Log validation + guarantee atomic insert Common anti-pattern fix: Restarting the database forcibly clears locks, but uncommitted suspended transactions prevent pending paid carts from ever being written. Who resolves it Senior backend engineer. Permanent resilience requires decoupling ingestion from execution via message queues: ingest webhook payload to broker first, then process asynchronously. Impact If Left Unresolved Every dropped webhook is a charged client with an empty basket. These remain invisible until chargebacks and support escalations arrive. metin: The client was billed twice for the same cart. A refund is mandatory, but isolating which tier duplicated the transaction is critical. Likely causes and fix. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy The client was billed twice for the same cart. A refund is mandatory, but isolating which tier duplicated the transaction is critical — patching the wrong layer allows duplicates to persist. Urgency: Critical · chargeback risk · Category: Orders & Payments Field Observations Moments after clicking purchase, the customer receives two consecutive bank deduction alerts. Only one order number appears in the dashboard; the customer reports double billing and files a chargeback with their bank. Observed System Error Signatures Two successful charges with identical payment reference Webhook logs: identical event ID processed twice App logs: two submissions, same second, same session Payment gateway dashboard shows no duplicate transaction alert Gateway transaction IDs and internal order tokens are distinct. Which one is duplicated indicates whether concurrency stems from client UI or webhook replays. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Client double submit Submit button was not disabled on click; slow response caused user double-click. Differential test: Did both requests originate from same session? Evidence: Two posts, same session → A Resolution: Button lock + idempotency key header Common anti-pattern fix: Disabling the button via JavaScript alone fails because submitting via the Enter key bypasses frontend guards without backend idempotency. B · Webhook redelivery Gateway redelivered standard retry callback. App treated both as novel transactions. Differential test: Was same event ID executed multiple times? Evidence: Same event ID processed twice → B Resolution: Record event ID · ignore duplicate callbacks Common anti-pattern fix: Increasing gateway timeout thresholds fails because the webhook handler still processes duplicate payloads without checking transaction references. C · Blind client retry App got network timeout and blindly retried transaction, unaware first attempt succeeded. Differential test: Did first attempt experience read timeout? Evidence: Retry after timeout → C Resolution: Safe retry logic · reuse identical idempotency key Common anti-pattern fix: When users press the browser back button, the session executes again; lacking single-use verification tokens allows the bank to reauthorize. Who resolves it Backend engineer. Scope, timeline and budget become clear after diagnosis. The root solution for all three is strict idempotency: ensuring identical payment attempts return identical cached results without multiple charges. Impact If Left Unresolved Refunds settle double charges but merchant processing fees and customer trust are permanently lost. Gateway risk algorithms penalize high chargeback accounts. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy Specific operations — checkout completion, stock updates, or batch imports — hang indefinitely until timeout. The server has not crashed; concurrent transactions are locked waiting for each other. Urgency: Critical · transaction halt · Category: Performance Field Observations When users submit forms or proceed to checkout, the browser tab spinner spins indefinitely. The page hangs white without showing errors; simultaneously, incoming visitors cannot even connect to the homepage. Observed System Error Signatures Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction → A · Cross-ordered row locks Lock wait timeout exceeded; try restarting transaction → B · Long-running transaction Database holds long-running idle in transaction locks → B · Long-running transaction App logs: two concurrent batch updates in same second 'try restarting transaction' is the database engine's explicit diagnosis. When logged, root cause is verified deadlock. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Cross-ordered row locks Two transactions update tables in reverse order; each blocks waiting for the other's release. Differential test: Are deadlock / lock wait errors present in logs? Evidence: Deadlock found in database log → A Resolution: Enforce global consistent lock acquisition order Common anti-pattern fix: Restarting the database service resets locks, but identical SQL transaction sequencing promptly deadlocks the tables under the next traffic burst. B · Long-running transaction Transaction wraps external API calls or PDF generation, holding database row locks for minutes. Differential test: Do open DB locks persist for multiple minutes? Evidence: Idle in transaction > 60s → B Resolution: Move external I/O outside of SQL transactions Common anti-pattern fix: Moving reporting queries to midnight fails over time as growing data sets spill into morning hours, freezing live transactional operations. C · Broad table lock (Batch) Nightly batch import locks wide index ranges, starving real-time checkout threads. Differential test: Do lock spikes overlap with cron batch execution? Evidence: Deadlock coincides with cron batch → C Resolution: Chunk batch updates + off-peak queue scheduling Common anti-pattern fix: Doubling worker pool limits fails because unaddressed database bottlenecks cause all newly spawned processes to lock and saturate within seconds. Who resolves it Senior backend engineer. Database engine outputs the conflicting queries in crash logs; resolution requires re-ordering table mutations and scoping transaction lifecycles. Impact If Left Unresolved Deadlocks compound during peak traffic campaigns. Their insidious nature is selective failure: catalogs browse fine while core checkout operations grind to a halt. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy Records vanish after a release, triggering data deletion panic. In most incidents, data remains intact; the query reading it mutated. Attempting hasty fixes without proper diagnosis risks causing genuine data loss. Urgency: Critical · data panic · Category: Data & Migration Field Observations Following a late-night release, store managers discover that recent orders, customer notes, or custom attributes vanished. Customer support calls asking 'Where is my order?' provide the first concrete evidence of lost data. Observed System Error Signatures Migration logs: rolled back or interrupted mid-execution → B · Interrupted schema migration Column not found / Unknown column in field list → B · Interrupted schema migration Row count: does table row count still match previous value? Were status or soft-delete flags updated in bulk? The first step is counting table rows directly. If row counts match, data is not erased; its visibility is filtered out. This distinction fundamentally changes the incident response vector. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Default query filter changed A new status column or soft-delete flag was added; legacy rows fail the default WHERE clause. Differential test: Is database row count identical to baseline? Evidence: Row count unchanged in DB → A Resolution: Backfill default flag on legacy records Common anti-pattern fix: Restoring a full database backup wipes out all legitimate new orders created between the migration event and the recovery attempt. B · Interrupted schema migration DDL migration halted mid-stream; half the tables are upgraded, causing joins to fail. Differential test: Did migration log terminate with an unhandled error? Evidence: Migration abort in deploy log → B Resolution: Restore snapshot · re-run clean migration script Common anti-pattern fix: Fixing database credentials in .env re-points future traffic, but legitimate customer records already written into staging remain abandoned and unmerged. C · Genuine bulk deletion A runaway script or bad WHERE clause executed actual hard DELETE. Rare, but the only true data loss scenario. Differential test: Did physical row count actually drop? Evidence: Row count decreased in DB → C Resolution: Point-in-time backup restore · time critical Common anti-pattern fix: Running Redis flushall purges volatile caches alongside unpersisted cart sessions sharing the same instance, destroying customer state irreversibly. Who resolves it The absolute first rule is freezing all writes. Writing new data or altering schemas destroys recovery options. Scope, timeline and budget become clear after diagnosis: B runs from backup, C requires immediate point-in-time snapshot recovery. Impact If Left Unresolved Under true deletion, the recovery window equals snapshot retention. The most frequent catastrophe is attempting blind repairs that overwrite restorable blocks. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy A new release went live and the site broke. The team wants to rollback but has no documented rollback plan. The critical failure is not the bug itself, but the lack of an atomic rollback mechanism. Urgency: Critical · deploy failure · Category: Live Outage Field Observations A release intended only to tweak a button label or style goes live. Instantly, checkout buttons disappear, CSS styling collapses, or the homepage fails entirely. The agency scrambles in panic to execute an emergency rollback. Observed System Error Signatures Deployment log: which version, timestamp, deployed by whom? Do new error signatures correlate with deploy timestamp? Static assets served from stale cache version Did database migrations execute alongside deploy? A crash coinciding with deployment timestamp pinpoints where to investigate. The primary question is never 'what changed', but 'can we immediately roll back'. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Missing build asset / vendor Artifact or composer/npm dependency omitted from build bundle. Present locally, missing on server. Differential test: Do logs show 404 / missing module fatal errors? Evidence: Class / file not found in logs → A Resolution: Deploy complete bundle · one-click rollback ready Common anti-pattern fix: Asking clients to clear browser cache fails because missing compiled dist asset bundles on the server prevent stylesheets from loading universally. B · Stale client / CDN cache HTML references new JS bundles while CDN or browser serves cached legacy files, causing partial rendering crashes. Differential test: Does Shift+F5 hard reload fix the page layout? Evidence: Hard refresh resolves visual glitch → B Resolution: Content hashing + automated CDN cache purge on deploy Common anti-pattern fix: Rushing a code rollback leaves half-migrated database schema alterations behind, causing fatal SQL exceptions on both current and legacy builds. C · Database schema desync Code expects newly added table columns but migration failed to run, or vice versa. Code rollback alone is insufficient. Differential test: Are SQL schema / missing column errors present? Evidence: Column not found SQL errors → C Resolution: Rollback schema + revert code synchronously Common anti-pattern fix: Overwriting production .env with a legacy backup deletes configuration keys required by newly deployed features, compounding the failure. Who resolves it Permanent reliability requires automated rollbacks: immutable git releases, content-hashed assets, and backward-compatible database migrations. When in place, a bad deploy is resolved in 60 seconds. Impact If Left Unresolved Un-rollbackable deployments breed release terror. Fear slows iteration cadence, causing massive batch releases that exponentially increase risk. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy A website that booted flawlessly yesterday throws 500 errors today, with team members insisting nothing changed. "Nothing changed" is almost always false — something mutated, just not necessarily code. Urgency: Critical · outage · Category: Live Outage Field Observations Overnight or at morning shift start, visitors hit an immediate blank screen or 500 error. Agency developers insist no code deployments occurred; the site appears to have collapsed spontaneously, triggering widespread panic. Observed System Error Signatures PHP Fatal error / Uncaught Error <- application logs 502 Bad Gateway · upstream prematurely closed connection → B · Disk / memory exhausted No space left on device → B · Disk / memory exhausted SQLSTATE[HY000] [2002] Connection refused → B · Disk / memory exhausted HTTP 500 is not a diagnosis; it is a generic wrapper. The actual root cause lives in application error logs one line below. Any guesswork without log inspection is wasted downtime. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Expired credentials An API key, database secret, or service account credential expired. Code remains untouched, but upstream authentication is failing. Differential test: Is there a 401 / auth failure in system logs? Evidence: Authentication failed in log → A Resolution: Secret rotation · fixed in mins Common anti-pattern fix: Repeatedly restarting web servers fails because connections remain impossible until expired API keys or database credentials are authenticated and rotated. B · Disk / memory exhausted Log files, automated dumps, or temp caches filled the disk partition; runtime writes fail. Differential test: Does df -h output show 100% disk utilization? Evidence: No space left on device → B Resolution: Disk sanitize + logrotate cron Common anti-pattern fix: Deleting application cache folders leaves unrotated log files in /var/log, causing the disk partition to hit 100 percent again shortly. C · Unattended OS update OS packages, shared libraries, or plugins auto-updated overnight. "Nobody touched it" is true; the daemon did. Differential test: Did unattended upgrades execute last night? Evidence: Nightly auto-update in apt/yum log → C Resolution: Package pinning + rollback patch Common anti-pattern fix: Running composer update pulls breaking major dependencies, exacerbating runtime incompatibility errors instead of restoring the prior working environment. Who resolves it A and B are sysadmin operations; scope, timeline and budget become clear after diagnosis. For C, the exact mutated package must be identified before executing rollbacks; reverting the wrong library causes secondary outages. Impact If Left Unresolved Search engine crawlers index HTTP 500 responses immediately. Prolonged downtime induces organic de-indexing, which takes far longer to recover than resolving the incident. Sisteminizde bu satırları görüyorsanız 403 Forbidden / sağlayıcının bakım veya askı sayfası E-posta kutusu: 'Payment failed' · 'Final notice' · 'Account suspended' DNS çözülüyor ama: Connection refused / 502 Bad Gateway İlk bakılacak yer sunucu değil, hesabın kayıtlı olduğu e-posta kutusudur. Sağlayıcılar askıya almadan önce genellikle birden fazla uyarı gönderir. Üç olası neden ve ayırt edici testleri A · Ödeme başarısız, hesap askıda Kartın süresi doldu ya da tahsilat başarısız oldu. Sağlayıcı uyarıları gönderdi, kimse okumadı. Teknik bir arıza yok. Ayırt edici test: Fatura adresine 'suspended' maili gelmiş mi? Kanıt: Kutuda 'suspended' maili var → A Çözüm: Ödeme + hesap sahibi Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Kart limiti apar topar artırılıp beklenir; ancak sağlayıcıya manuel ödeme bildirimi yapılmadığı için askı durumu saatlerce devam eder. B · Kaynak kotası doldu Bant genişliği, disk veya CPU limiti aşıldı. Hesap askıda değil, kota kilidinde. Ödeme sorunu değildir. Ayırt edici test: Panelde disk / bant genişliği %100 mü? Kanıt: Panelde kullanım %100 → B Çözüm: Plan yükseltme veya kaynak optimizasyonu Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Destek bileti açılarak faturaya itiraz edilir; fakat sızan anahtar silinip yetkiler iptal edilmediği sürece güvenlik ekibi hesabı kesinlikle açmaz. C · Kötüye kullanım bildirimi Site ele geçirilmiş, spam veya zararlı içerik dağıtıyor olabilir. Sağlayıcı güvenlik gerekçesiyle kapatmıştır. Ayırt edici test: abuse@ adresine bildirim gelmiş mi? Kanıt: abuse bildirimi var → C Çözüm: ÖNCE güvenlik temizliği, SONRA askı kaldırma Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Muhasebe departmanına yeni bildirim maili tanımlanır; ancak eski faturalar ödenip sağlayıcı onayı alınmadığı için dondurulan hizmetler aktifleşmez. Kim çözer A ise hesap sahibi ve muhasebe — kod işi değildir. B ise sistem yöneticisi. C ise güvenlik müdahalesi gerekir ve sıra bağlayıcıdır: temizlik yapılmadan askı kaldırılırsa hesap tekrar kapatılır. Çözülmezse ne olur Sağlayıcılar askıya alınan hesapların verisini belirli bir süre saklar, sonra kalıcı olarak siler. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy The application became completely unreachable out of nowhere. No code changes, no deployments, no manual changes. The root cause is almost never within code — and every hour spent looking in the wrong place increases catastrophic data loss risk. Urgency: Critical · outage · Category: Infrastructure & Access Field Observations On a Monday morning, logins to AWS, Google Cloud, or DigitalOcean fail; live instances, databases, and company emails are down. The dashboard displays a red 'Account Suspended' banner. The entire digital operation is paralyzed at once. Observed System Error Signatures 403 Forbidden / provider maintenance or suspension page Inbox: 'Payment failed' · 'Final notice' · 'Account suspended' DNS resolves but: Connection refused / 502 Bad Gateway The first place to inspect is not server logs, but the root billing email inbox. Cloud providers virtually always dispatch multiple pre-suspension notices. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Billing failure / suspended Card expired or bank transaction declined. Provider dispatched warnings that went unread. Zero technical defect. Differential test: Was a suspended email sent to billing address? Evidence: Suspension email in inbox → A Resolution: Payment update + account holder Common anti-pattern fix: Increasing card limits without manually triggering repayment in the billing console leaves account suspensions active for hours. B · Quota / resource limit Bandwidth, disk volume, or CPU throttle limits reached. Account is not delinquent, but throttled by quotas. Differential test: Is disk or bandwidth usage at 100% cap? Evidence: Dashboard usage 100% → B Resolution: Plan tier upgrade or resource optimization Common anti-pattern fix: Disputing charges via support tickets stalls indefinitely because cloud security teams refuse reinstatement until compromised keys and malicious instances are removed. C · Abuse notice / security lock Application was compromised, sending spam or malicious outbound traffic. Provider hard-locked access for policy violations. Differential test: Was notice sent to abuse / root mailbox? Evidence: Abuse report in inbox → C Resolution: Security sanitize FIRST, then request unlock Common anti-pattern fix: Updating billing recipient emails fails to restore service until outstanding invoices are settled and reviewed by cloud risk teams. Who resolves it For A: Account owner and accounting — zero coding required. For B: DevOps / Sysadmin. For C: Forensic security SWAT is required with strict sequencing: requesting unban prior to full cleanup triggers instant re-suspension. Impact If Left Unresolved Cloud providers retain suspended account storage only for a specific grace window before permanent, unrecoverable disk sanitization. If no external backup exists, recovery is impossible. Aciliyet: Kritik · veri riski · Kategori: Devir & Süreklilik Sahada nasıl görünür Veritabanı silindiğinde veya sunucu çöktüğünde hosting panelindeki 'Otomatik Yedekler' klasörüne güvenle girilir. Ancak dosya boyutu sıfır bayt çıkar, arşiv bozuktur veya son yedek altı ay öncesine aittir; panik içinde gerçek anlaşılır. Sisteminizde bu satırları görüyorsanız Yedek klasöründeki son dosyanın tarihi ← aylar öncesi mi? cron log: backup job — exit status 1 → A · Yedek alınmıyor Yedek dosya boyutu 0 byte / birkaç KB Depolama sağlayıcısı: quota exceeded → A · Yedek alınmıyor Yedek işi çoğu zaman sessizce başarısız olur. Hata bir yere düşer ama kimse okumaz; klasörde dosya göründüğü için sorun fark edilmez. Üç olası neden ve ayırt edici testleri A · Yedek alınmıyor Görev kurulmuş ama çalışmıyor: zamanlayıcı durmuş, kimlik değişmiş ya da hedef dolmuş. Ayırt edici test: Son yedek dosyası kaç günlük? Kanıt: Son yedek tarihi çok eski → A Çözüm: Görev onarımı + başarısızlık bildirimi Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Cron dosyasına yeni bir mysqldump komutu eklenir; ancak dump dosyası boş bir veritabanına yüklenip test edilmediğinden yedeğin çalıştığı kanıtlanamaz. B · Yedek eksik alınıyor Dosyalar var ama veritabanı yok, ya da tersi. Kısmi yedek olay anında tam geri dönüş sağlamaz. Ayırt edici test: Yedekte veritabanı dökümü var mı? Kanıt: Yedekte veritabanı dökümü yok → B Çözüm: Kapsam genişletme + boyut kontrolü Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Yedekler aynı sunucunun /backup dizinine kaydedilir; fiziksel disk bozulduğunda veya sanal sunucu silindiğinde hem canlı sistem hem de yedekler yok olur. C · Geri yüklenemiyor Dosya bozuk, şifresi kayıp ya da sürüm uyumsuz. Hiç denenmediği için bugüne kadar bilinmiyordu. Ayırt edici test: Boş ortama geri yükleme denendi mi? Kanıt: Test geri yükleme başarısız → C Çözüm: Düzenli geri yükleme provası Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Veritabanı tabloları kilitlenmeden canlı dump alınır; transaction tutarlılığı sağlanmadığı için dosyadan geri yüklenen veritabanı yarım tablolar yüzünden açılamaz. Kim çözer Sistem yöneticisi. Ama asıl çözüm teknik değil rutinseldir: yedek başarısız olduğunda haber veren bir bildirim ve düzenli aralıklarla yapılan geri yükleme provası. baslik: Backup Assumed to Exist, No Valid Backup
metin: An outage occurred, a rollback to backup was requested, only to discover snapshots were never generated or are un-restorable. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy An outage occurred, a rollback to backup was requested, only to discover snapshots were never generated or are un-restorable. A backup file existing versus being restorable are entirely different; the latter is unknown until tested. Urgency: Critical · data loss risk · Category: Handover & Continuity Field Observations After database corruption or a server crash, administrators confidently open automated backup archives. Only then do they discover zero-byte files, corrupt tarballs, or dumps dating back six months; panic ensues. Observed System Error Signatures Last backup file timestamp in directory <- months outdated? cron log: backup job — exit status 1 → A · Backups not running Backup archive size 0 bytes / empty archive Storage provider: quota exceeded → A · Backups not running Backup routines fail silently most of the time. Errors are emitted to unmonitored logs while stale files in the folder give a false sense of security. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Backups not running Cron was configured but terminated: scheduler daemon died, auth expired, or target bucket filled up. Differential test: How old is the latest backup file in storage? Evidence: Latest backup date is stale → A Resolution: Cron repair + dead-man switch alerts Common anti-pattern fix: Adding fresh mysqldump cron jobs proves meaningless without automated test restores into staging to verify dump integrity. B · Partial / incomplete dump Uploaded assets exist without SQL dumps, or vice versa. Partial snapshots prevent full recovery during disaster recovery. Differential test: Does archive contain valid SQL dump file? Evidence: Missing SQL dump in archive → B Resolution: Full scope dump + file size threshold check Common anti-pattern fix: Storing dumps in local /backup directories guarantees total data loss when underlying disks fail or hypervisor instances terminate. C · Un-restorable / corrupted Archive is corrupt, decryption key is missing, or schema versions clash. Never tested until live disaster hit. Differential test: Was restore tested in clean sandbox env? Evidence: Test sandbox restore failed → C Resolution: Automated drill restoration in staging sandbox Common anti-pattern fix: Taking database dumps without single-transaction flags produces fractured relational states that fail integrity checks during emergency recovery imports. Who resolves it Sysadmin / DevOps. But the true solution is procedural: dead-man failure alerts and scheduled sandbox restoration drills. An untested backup is not a backup. Impact If Left Unresolved Every day operating without restorable backups is a single disk crash or rogue query away from total business termination. Aciliyet: Kritik · güven kaybı · Kategori: Altyapı & Erişim Sahada nasıl görünür Sabah saatlerinde siteye giren müşteriler tarayıcıda 'Bağlantınız Gizli Değil' kırmızı ekran uyarısıyla karşılaşır. Üç olası neden ve ayırt edici testleri A · Yenileme durdu Kısa ömürlü sertifikalar otomatik yenilenir; yenileme görevi bir noktada sessizce durmuştur. Ayırt edici test: Yenileme görevi çalışıyor mu? Kanıt: Yenileme log'unda hata → A Çözüm: Görev onarımı + süre bildirimi Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Web sunucusuna yeni bir sertifika yüklenip bırakılır; sunucu servisi yeniden başlatılmadığı için aktif bağlantılar eski süresi geçmiş sertifikayı sunmayı sürdürür. B · Kapsam eksik Sertifika ana alan adını kapsıyor ama `www` veya bir alt alan adını kapsamıyor. Ayırt edici test: Hata kodu CN / alan adı hatası mı? Kanıt: COMMON_NAME hatası → B Çözüm: Sertifikayı alt alan adlarıyla yeniden al Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Certbot komutu elle çalıştırılır; yenileme cron tablosu veya webroot erişim yetkisi düzeltilmediği için sertifika üç ay sonra sessizce tekrar süresi dolar. C · Zincir eksik Sertifika geçerli ama zincir tamamlanmamış. Bazı cihazlarda çalışır, bazılarında çalışmaz — en yanıltıcı hâl budur. Ayırt edici test: Bazı cihazlarda çalışıp bazılarında çalışmıyor mu? Kim çözer Sistem yöneticisi. Kapsam, süre ve bütçe teşhisten sonra netleşir. Asıl mesele tekrarını önlemektir: yenileme başarısız olduğunda haber veren bir bildirim kurulmadıkça aynı arıza sertifika ömrü kadar sonra geri gelir. baslik: SSL Certificate Expired, Security Warning Displayed
metin: Users are blocked by 'Your connection is not private' browser interstitials. The application is running fine, but the TLS handshake fails. SSL Certificate Expired, Security Warning Displayed Home Services & Engagement Model Capacity & Infrastructure Agency Kit Crash Test (60s) Handover Audit tmai Diagnostic Catalog Salvageability Index Post-Mortem & RCA Triage Simulator SLA & Commitments Tech Matrix Mutual NDA Confidentiality and Engagement Agreement Damage Simulator Status Radar Codebase Health Rescue or Rebuild? Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy Users are blocked by 'Your connection is not private' browser interstitials. The application is running fine, but the TLS handshake fails. Clients perceive a breach; technically it is usually a stalled renewal script. Urgency: Critical · trust loss · Category: Infrastructure & Access Field Observations In the morning hours, visitors entering the site encounter red 'Your connection is not private' browser interstitials. Seeing the security warning, customers abandon carts immediately rather than submitting payment details; support desks are flooded with complaints asking if the site was compromised. Observed System Error Signatures NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID <- certificate expired → A · Auto-renewal stopped NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID <- hostname mismatch → B · Missing SAN / subdomains SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate → C · Incomplete CA chain certbot renew — hook command failed → A · Auto-renewal stopped Browser error codes state the exact root cause directly. The 'Advanced' button reveals whether expiration, domain mismatch, or broken CA chain is at play. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Auto-renewal stopped Automated 90-day certificates require active cron hooks; the renewal task failed silently without triggering alerts. Differential test: Is certbot / ACME cron executing cleanly? Evidence: Certbot renewal error in log → A Resolution: Certbot repair + expiry monitoring webhook Common anti-pattern fix: Installing new certificates without reloading the web server daemon leaves active listener processes serving the expired certificate. B · Missing SAN / subdomains Certificate covers apex domain but lacks SAN coverage for `www` or target subdomains. Differential test: Is error code COMMON_NAME mismatch? Evidence: COMMON_NAME_INVALID error → B Resolution: Re-issue with all SAN / www subdomains Common anti-pattern fix: Running certbot manually renews the certificate once but fails to fix cron triggers or webroot permissions, ensuring recurrence ninety days later. C · Incomplete CA chain Leaf certificate is valid but intermediate CA bundle is missing. Works on modern desktops, fails on mobile — the most deceptive failure. Differential test: Does it fail only on specific mobile clients? Evidence: unable to get local issuer error → C Resolution: Install fullchain bundle to web server config Common anti-pattern fix: Re-pointing DNS records directly to origin servers leaves CDN proxy layers serving cached expired edge certificates to incoming clients. Who resolves it DevOps / Sysadmin. Scope, timeline and budget become clear after diagnosis. The true goal is preventing recurrence: without a notification that fires when renewal fails, the same failure returns once the certificate's lifetime runs out. Impact If Left Unresolved Most visitors turn back when they see a browser security warning. On a checkout page, that warning means the day's sales stop. Üç olası neden ve ayırt edici testleri A · Sorgu çoğalması Listedeki her satır için ayrı sorgu atılıyor. 10 kayıtla fark edilmez, 500 kayıtla site durur. B · Dizin eksik Sorgu doğru ama tablo baştan sona taranıyor. Veri büyüdükçe süre doğrusal artar. Ayırt edici test: Yavaş sorgu tüm tabloyu mu tarıyor? Kanıt: Yavaş sorgu tüm tabloyu tarıyor → B Çözüm: Dizin ekle · etki anında Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: PHP yapılandırmasında max_execution_time süresi artırılır; bu işlem yanıt vermeyen kargo veya SMS servisinin tüm PHP-FPM havuzunu tıkamasına yol açar. C · Harici bekleme Kargo, ödeme veya stok servisi yavaş yanıt veriyor ve sayfa onu bekliyor. Ayırt edici test: Yavaşlık harici çağrıda mı yoğunlaşıyor? Kim çözer Kıdemli backend mühendisi. Kapsam, süre ve bütçe teşhisten sonra netleşir; A ve B kapandığında etkisi anında görülür. C'de asıl mesele harici servisi hızlandırmak değil, sayfanın onu beklememesini sağlamaktır. Çözülmezse ne olur Yavaşlık dönüşümü doğrudan düşürür ve arama sıralamasında da karşılığı vardır. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy Page latency surges while server CPU and RAM remain idle. Upgrading infrastructure tiers changes nothing. Sluggish performance on idle servers is a blocking I/O bottleneck, not a compute limitation. Urgency: High · conversion loss · Category: Performance Field Observations Visitors complain that pages take fifteen seconds to load or time out completely. Looking at htop or top shows CPU and RAM below five percent, practically idling; the origin of the freeze remains baffling. Observed System Error Signatures Database queries per page load: hundreds of queries Slow query log: identical query repeated dozens of times External 3rd-party API call: 2-8s blocking latency Time to First Byte (TTFB) high, download payload fast Latency with low CPU indicates blocking wait states. The metric to investigate is not CPU utilization, but where the thread is blocking. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · N+1 query explosion Loop triggers separate SQL queries for each item. Unnoticeable with 10 items, catastrophic with 500. Differential test: Does same query execute hundreds of times per hit? Evidence: Same query loops hundreds of times → A Resolution: Eager loading + batch SQL joins Common anti-pattern fix: Upgrading server CPU and RAM fails because an unindexed SELECT query locks the entire table regardless of hardware capacity. B · Missing database index Query syntax is clean but triggers full table scans (Seq Scan). Duration grows linearly with table size. Differential test: Does EXPLAIN show full table scan on large tables? Evidence: Full table scan in EXPLAIN log → B Resolution: Add composite index · instant speedup Common anti-pattern fix: Increasing max_execution_time backfires by allowing unresponsive third-party shipping or SMS APIs to exhaust the entire PHP-FPM process pool. C · Synchronous third-party I/O Outbound carrier, payment, or ERP API is slow and web process blocks execution. Differential test: Is TTFB spent on outbound 3rd-party HTTP requests? Evidence: Latency concentrated in external cURL → C Resolution: Redis cache + strict timeouts + async background Common anti-pattern fix: Raising max_connections indefinitely forces MySQL into swap under memory pressure, locking the server down at the OS level. Who resolves it Senior backend engineer. Scope, timeline and budget become clear after diagnosis; once A and B are resolved, the speedup is immediate. For C, the solution is asynchronous decoupling so pages never block on third parties. Impact If Left Unresolved High latency degrades checkout conversion and organic Core Web Vitals. Server upgrades mask symptoms temporarily while increasing cloud spend without fixing root flaws. Kanıt: İstek sayısı zamanla artmış → A Çözüm: Toplu istek + paket yükseltme Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: İstekler arasına kısa sleep() komutları eklenir; kuyrukta bekleyen siparişler arttıkça cron her çalıştığında dakikalık kota yine dakikalar içinde aşılır. B · Döngüsel tekrar Hata sonrası yeniden deneme mantığı beklemeden tekrarlıyor ve limiti kendi kendine dolduruyor. Ayırt edici test: Aynı istek çok kısa aralıkla mı tekrarlıyor? Kanıt: Aynı istek çok kısa aralıkla tekrarlıyor → B Çözüm: Artan bekleme süresi ekle Sık yapılan yanlış düzeltme: Cron sıklığı on dakikaya çıkarılır; bu kez müşteriye takip numarası saatlerce gecikir ancak API limiti ilk toplu işlemde tekrar patlar. C · Limit değişti Karşı taraf kotayı değiştirdi ya da fiyat planı düştü. Sizde hiçbir şey değişmedi. Ayırt edici test: Limit başlığındaki değer düştü mü? Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy An integration running smoothly for months — carrier, marketplace, payment gateway, or transactional email — abruptly fails with HTTP 429. The remote host is throttling your traffic due to volumetric burst limits. Urgency: High · data sync halted · Category: Contact & Integrations Field Observations E-commerce modules communicating with marketplaces, couriers, or SMS providers halt abruptly. Orders fail to sync, admin dashboards warn 'Service unreachable', and the integration partner claims minute request quotas were exceeded. Observed System Error Signatures HTTP 429 Too Many Requests Retry-After: 60 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 Provider dashboard: quota exceeded for this period The Retry-After header indicates the mandatory cooldown interval. Retrying blindly without parsing backoff headers prolongs IP ban windows. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Natural volume growth Order volume scaled naturally, exceeding baseline API tier quota without notice. Differential test: Has API traffic grown steadily in recent months? Evidence: Request rate climbed over time → A Resolution: Batch payloads + upgrade API tier Common anti-pattern fix: Adding naive sleep() calls between requests fails because accumulated queue backlogs inevitably blow through rate limits on subsequent cron runs. B · Retry storm (No backoff) Worker catches transient error and immediately hammers API in tight loop, exhausting rate limits. Differential test: Are retry requests fired without backoff delays? Evidence: Rapid repeated requests in log → B Resolution: Exponential backoff + jitter retry logic Common anti-pattern fix: Reducing cron frequency to ten minutes delays tracking numbers for hours while still exhausting API quotas during bulk sync spikes. C · Provider quota downgrade Upstream provider tightened throttle policy or subscription plan lapsed to free tier. Differential test: Did rate limit header cap drop unexpectedly? Evidence: X-RateLimit cap dropped in headers → C Resolution: Negotiate higher tier with vendor Common anti-pattern fix: Copying production API credentials to staging backfires when automated QA scripts exhaust the organization's hourly quota within minutes. Who resolves it Backend engineer. Permanent resilience combines payload batching with exponential backoff and jitter algorithms. This enables integrations to scale gracefully with traffic spikes. Impact If Left Unresolved Throttled requests mean desynchronized operations: tracking numbers unsent, inventory un-updated, customer transactional emails lost in queue. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy The application slows down or freezes predictably every afternoon; rebooting restores normal function. Daily reboots are not a solution but a temporary band-aid — with degradation creeping earlier every day. Urgency: High · masked defect · Category: Infrastructure & Access Field Observations The system bogs down daily at similar hours and relies on a nightly cron reboot to stay alive. Customers notice snappy mornings but sluggish checkout afternoons; the failure has become routine yet remains unresolved. Observed System Error Signatures Out of memory: Killed process Memory consumption climbs steadily without dropping Process manager (PM2): daily restart count increasing Response latencies degrade progressively during peak hours Memory utilization graphs provide instant diagnosis: sawtooth patterns reflect healthy garbage collection; monotonic linear ascent proves memory leaks. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Application memory leak Unbounded caches or unclosed references accumulate until Linux OOM killer terminates the process. Differential test: Does RAM graph ever drop during idle periods? Evidence: RAM usage never drops → A Resolution: Heap dump profile + patch leak Common anti-pattern fix: Scheduling twice-daily reboots fails because leaky code cycles continue exhausting RAM during sudden mid-day traffic surges. B · Unbuffered export spike Bulk CSV export loads entire 500k row database into memory buffer at once, triggering instant OOM. Differential test: Do memory spikes correlate with bulk export jobs? Evidence: Crash coincides with heavy report → B Resolution: Stream chunking + generator buffer Common anti-pattern fix: Manually purging temp directories with rm -rf fails because missing logrotate configurations allow multi-gigabyte log dumps to exhaust disk space again. C · Genuine capacity ceiling Zero memory leaks; active concurrent user count simply exceeded instance memory limits. Differential test: Is RAM steady high proportional to active users? Evidence: Stable high load proportional to traffic → C Resolution: Scale instance RAM · valid upgrade Common anti-pattern fix: Indiscriminately terminating tasks with killall -9 leaves orphaned database sockets hanging, locking connection pools on the very next cycle. Who resolves it A and B are application bugs; automated cron reboots mask them without fixing. C is legitimate hardware scaling — but upgrading before diagnosing A & B wastes cloud spend while crashes persist. Impact If Left Unresolved Daily reboots inevitably degrade into multi-hour crashes during high-traffic campaign peaks. It is a scheduled disaster waiting to execute. baslik: Works in Staging, Fails in Production
metin: The developer says 'it works on my machine' and they are correct. In production, identical code behaves differently. Likely causes and the fix. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy The developer says 'it works on my machine' and they are correct. In production, identical code behaves differently. This is environment drift, not a developer competency flaw. Urgency: High · release blocker · Category: Handover & Continuity Field Observations Developers provide screen recordings demonstrating flawless functionality on local and staging servers. Yet the moment code hits production, blank screens, 500 errors, or missing data appear, triggering finger-pointing between teams. Observed System Error Signatures Undefined env variable / configuration missing → A · Configuration drift Fails with 500 only on production, passes 200 on staging Dependency versions: lockfile present and synchronized? Permission denied - file permissions or path mismatch → C · Permissions / path discrepancy Environment drift always lives in one of three places: configuration, dependency versions, or file permissions. Searching elsewhere wastes critical incident time. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Configuration drift Production environment variable missing or set to invalid endpoint. Same code, differing inputs. Differential test: Is an environment variable missing in production? Evidence: Missing .env in production → A Resolution: Sync .env schema + track .env.example in git Common anti-pattern fix: Manually copying script files to staging overlooks discrepancies in PHP extensions or MySQL strict mode flags between the two server runtimes. B · Dependency / runtime mismatch Language or package minor versions differ between environments. Unlocked package versions drifted. Differential test: Are lockfile package versions identical across tiers? Evidence: Version mismatch in lockfile → B Resolution: Commit strict package-lock / composer.lock Common anti-pattern fix: Hardcoding missing environment variables directly into application logic fails when credentials rotate or repositories are deployed to new infrastructure. C · Permissions / path discrepancy Target directory lacks write permissions on production web server, or hardcoded absolute path fails. Differential test: Does log show EACCES / permission denied errors? Evidence: Permission denied in production log → C Resolution: Fix chmod permissions + load dynamic paths Common anti-pattern fix: Validating queries on ten mock records fails to reveal that production tables with hundreds of thousands of rows exhaust PHP memory. Who resolves it Backend / DevOps. Permanent stability comes from Infrastructure as Code and immutable container recipes; patching discrepancies ad-hoc leaves every future release vulnerable. Impact If Left Unresolved Every deployment becomes a high-stakes gamble. Teams dread pushing to prod, backlogs swell, and large batch deploys magnify catastrophic blast radiuses. baslik: Every New Feature Breaks an Existing Feature
metin: Fixing one module breaks another unrelated area. The development team repeatedly patches the same recurring bugs. Likely causes and the fix. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy Fixing one module breaks another unrelated area. The development team repeatedly patches the same recurring bugs. This is not developer negligence, but architectural fragility from accumulated technical debt. Urgency: High · technical debt · Category: Code Health Field Observations Implementing a requested payment method breaks automated invoicing; fixing invoicing disables discount coupons. The team spends days patching yesterday's side effects while introducing fresh defects, bringing feature delivery to a standstill. Observed System Error Signatures Regression: identical bug ticket reopened across sprints No automated test coverage, or tests skipped in CI God class anti-pattern: single source file spans thousands of lines Duplicate logic copy-pasted across multiple modules The only objective metric is bug regression frequency. 'Code feels bad' is subjective sentiment; 'the same checkout defect reopened four times in 90 days' is actionable data. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Duplicated business logic Identical calculation logic copy-pasted across multiple controllers. Fixing one leaves the others broken. Differential test: Is business logic duplicated in multiple controllers? Evidence: Duplicated algorithms in codebase → A Resolution: Consolidate to single service class · incremental Common anti-pattern fix: Nesting additional if-else branches into bloated functions magnifies cyclomatic complexity, guaranteeing future regressions across adjacent business logic. B · Missing regression test suite Zero automated unit/integration tests exist; side effects are discovered only after real customers encounter crashes. Differential test: Do automated tests cover critical checkout paths? Evidence: Zero test coverage in CI pipeline → B Resolution: Write regression tests on critical flows FIRST Common anti-pattern fix: Relying entirely on manual smoke testing fails because human fatigue inevitably misses edge cases across unverified adjacent modules. C · High module coupling Tightly coupled components mutate shared global state; altering one class triggers unpredictable cascade breaks. Differential test: Does localized edit break unrelated views? Evidence: Minor patch creates wide blast radius → C Resolution: Decouple boundaries via interfaces · step by step Common anti-pattern fix: Renaming conflicting global variables merely shifts unintended state mutation to other templates without isolating runtime scopes. Who resolves it Senior software architect. Sequence is mandatory: write regression tests FIRST, then refactor. Refactoring without test safety nets introduces secondary defects. Total rewrites from scratch are almost never the correct strategy. Impact If Left Unresolved Development velocity stalls exponentially. Simple features take weeks, engineering morale plummets, and external stakeholders perceive the engineering team as ineffective. B · Kaynak kod kayıp Sürüm kontrolü hiç kurulmamış. Canlı sunucudaki dosyalar tek kopya. En kırılgan hâl budur. Ayırt edici test: Sürüm kontrolü (git) var mı? Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy The developer who built the platform departed. The site continues running but cannot be modified: repository location, server SSH credentials, or account ownership remain unknown. These are three distinct bottlenecks, identifiable within hour one. Urgency: High · continuity risk · Category: Handover & Continuity Field Observations The sole developer behind the project departs or cuts communication. When emergency updates arise, the agency discovers nobody holds Git repo permissions, server keys, or deployment credentials; the company is locked out of its own software. Observed System Error Signatures git log -1 --format=%cd <- timestamp of last commit? git log --format='%an' | sort -u <- how many contributors touched code? ~/.ssh/authorized_keys <- who has SSH keys to production? WHOIS + cloud account <- registered to which email? These four checkpoints determine whether handover failure is technical or administrative. In most cases, the bottleneck is account ownership rather than code. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Loss of access Domain registrar, host, and git repos are registered to personal emails. Code and infrastructure are sound; the bottleneck is credential handover. Differential test: Are accounts tied to company domain email? Evidence: Accounts on personal mail → A Resolution: Account transfer — admin workflow, no coding needed Common anti-pattern fix: Requesting passwords via messaging apps fails when outdated credentials run straight into two-factor authentication prompts on personal devices. B · Missing source repository Version control was never initialized. Live production server contains the sole surviving copy. The highest-risk state. Differential test: Is version control (git remote) present? Evidence: No remote repo → B Resolution: Full live image FIRST, then git init setup Common anti-pattern fix: Tasking a replacement developer to reverse-engineer environment setups wastes days resolving undocumented build flags and missing local dependencies. C · Undocumented environment Repository exists but cannot be booted: setup commands, environment variables, and lockfiles are absent. Differential test: Are README and package lockfiles available? Evidence: Missing .env / lockfile → C Resolution: Environment rebuild + documentation Common anti-pattern fix: Downloading production files via FTP yields minified bundles; lacking original source code makes subsequent feature updates and debugging impractical. Who resolves it A is an administrative process, requiring zero coding. For B, the absolute first step is pulling a full live server image, not writing code. C is precisely what a handover code audit diagnoses. Impact If Left Unresolved Without version control, production is a single point of total failure. If the instance crashes, recovery is impossible. Risk compounds daily until full image verification is completed. Evidence: Personal email in WHOIS → A Resolution: Direct transfer · fast if contact is open Common anti-pattern fix: Terminating a former employee's corporate inbox cuts off password reset links for domain panels registered under that address. B · Held by third-party agency Domain purchased via third-party agency reseller pool. Owned in their account rather than client direct legal entity. Differential test: Is registrar tied to reseller agency name? Evidence: Registrant is reseller entity → B Resolution: EPP auth code + registrant transfer request Common anti-pattern fix: Engaging in informal disputes with former agencies fails; registrars require formal corporate authorization and legal release documents to transfer domains. C · Unreachable registrant Registrant mailbox abandoned, account holder unresponsive. Official registrar legal escalation required. Differential test: Does registrant mailbox receive inbound mail? Evidence: Bouncing mailbox / ghosted → C Resolution: Registrar recovery · corporate legal docs required Common anti-pattern fix: Calling registrar phone support achieves nothing without submitting notarized corporate authorization documents and official company registry certificates. Who resolves it This is an administrative and legal challenge; developers are not required initially. Corporate tax registration, invoice trails, and trademark certificates accelerate registrar transfer. Impact If Left Unresolved When domain expiration hits, the website drops overnight and can be snapped up by domain squatters, permanently destroying brand equity. metin: Lead or quote forms display 'Submitted successfully' but notifications never arrive in the team inbox. Likely causes and the fix. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy Lead or quote forms display 'Submitted successfully' but notifications never arrive in the team inbox. The most insidious defect: silence leaves lost deals completely untracked. Urgency: High · lost leads · Category: Contact & Integrations Field Observations Visitors submit quote forms and receive a cheerful 'Message sent successfully' banner. Yet nothing arrives in corporate inboxes. The failure operates in total silence; how many high-value leads were lost only becomes apparent weeks later. Observed System Error Signatures SMTP error 535 Authentication failed → A · SMTP auth failure 550 5.7.1 Message rejected · SPF / DKIM → B · Missing SPF / DKIM Mail queue: deferred / stuck → B · Missing SPF / DKIM App logs: 'mail sent' <- but never delivered by MTA 'Message sent' in UI only reflects dispatch, not inbox delivery. Truth resides in server mail queues (Postfix/Exim) or transactional ESP dashboards (SendGrid/Postmark). Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · SMTP auth failure Mailbox password expired or ESP enforced App Passwords/OAuth. Dispatch fails at origin. Differential test: Is there an SMTP 535 auth error in system logs? Evidence: SMTP 535 Authentication failed in log → A Resolution: App Password + config update in .env Common anti-pattern fix: Reverting to native PHP mail() dispatches unauthenticated envelopes that destination mail exchangers quietly quarantine or drop entirely. B · Missing SPF / DKIM Mail leaves server but destination MX rejects or junk-folders it due to missing SPF/DKIM/DMARC TXT records. Differential test: Are SPF and DKIM TXT records active in DNS? Evidence: 550 5.7.1 SPF/DKIM rejected → B Resolution: Add DNS records · deliverability restored Common anti-pattern fix: Injecting the submitter's email into the RFC-5322 From header triggers DMARC alignment failures, causing destination servers to reject delivery. C · False positive frontend AJAX endpoint returns 4xx/5xx but frontend ignores HTTP status and shows optimistic success alert. Differential test: Does network tab show HTTP 200 on POST request? Evidence: Network tab shows 4xx/5xx → C Resolution: Handle status · render error UI on failure Common anti-pattern fix: Masking frontend errors without checking server logs maintains a false sense of success while API endpoints continue throwing 500 exceptions. Who resolves it A and B are DNS/Sysadmin issues. C is frontend defect that must be solved first: false-positive success toasts hide lead bleed for months. Impact If Left Unresolved Every lost form is a lost deal that nobody knows was missed. This defect never announces itself; it bleeds revenue in silence. metin: The site is accessible and looks normal, but organic search rankings plummeted. Three likely causes, the test that tells them apart, and the fix. Downtime Calculator Technical Glossary Our Story Emergency Support About Us Privacy Policy The site is accessible and looks normal, but organic search rankings plummeted. Technical causes can be verified far faster than content or algorithmic penalties — rule them out first. Urgency: High · traffic loss · Category: Visibility Field Observations The website loads normally in browsers, leading teams to assume all is well. Yet searching the brand on Google yields zero results on page one. Daily organic traffic drops toward zero and inbound inquiries abruptly cease. Observed System Error Signatures robots.txt → Disallow: / → B · robots.txt blocked <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> → A · Staging noindex leaked Server response: 5xx errors or excessively slow TTFB Redirect chain loop: 302 -> 302 -> 200 The first two directives alone remove the entire site from search results, and they are usually carried over from the test environment to production by mistake. Takes seconds to verify. Three Potential Root Causes & Differential Tests A · Staging noindex leaked Robots noindex tag used to hide staging was mistakenly deployed to production release. Differential test: Is <meta noindex> present in HTML source? Evidence: Meta noindex found in DOM → A Resolution: Strip tag + request Google re-indexing Common anti-pattern fix: Publishing fresh content fails completely because search crawlers obey the meta noindex tag and refuse to index the URL. B · robots.txt blocked robots.txt file instructs all crawlers to disallow indexation across root. Differential test: Does robots.txt contain Disallow: root slash? Evidence: robots.txt Disallow: / → B Resolution: Fix rule · recovery on re-crawl Common anti-pattern fix: Resubmitting XML sitemaps achieves nothing while a rogue Disallow: / rule in robots.txt instructs search engine crawlers to abandon indexation. C · Broken 301 migrations URL architecture was revamped without 301 redirects. Legacy URLs return 404, wiping historical domain authority. Differential test: Do legacy URLs return 301 to new counterparts? Evidence: Legacy URLs return 404 → C Resolution: Deploy complete 301 redirect map table Common anti-pattern fix: Wildcard-redirecting old URLs to the homepage fails to transfer accumulated page-level ranking authority, resulting in massive organic traffic erosion. Who resolves it For A and B, scope, timeline and budget become clear after diagnosis; index restoration occurs when search engines re-crawl the site. C requires comprehensive URL mapping tables to preserve link equity. Impact If Left Unresolved Organic visibility drop compounds over time. Re-ranking takes significantly longer than the downtime duration — early mitigation protects top-line revenue.
